memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the Lord, the Eternal God. And Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines for a long time. - Gen 21:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a beautiful picture. Abraham plants a tree - a tamarisk, a slow-growing tree that would outlast him, a sign of taking root and looking to the future. And there he worships, calling on "the Lord, the Eternal God." This is the first time God is named this way in Scripture - El Olam, the Everlasting God, the God of eternity.

There is something fitting about this name coming here. Abraham had waited so long for the promise, lived through so many changes and uncertainties, and now, holding his promised son at last, he worships the God who is eternal - the God who was faithful across all those long years and who will be faithful forever. Above all the shifting circumstances of his life stood the unchanging, everlasting God.

This is a profound anchor for the soul. Everything in our lives is temporary and changing - our circumstances, our strength, our very days. But God is the Eternal God. He does not change, does not age, does not fail. "From everlasting to everlasting you are God" (Ps 90:2). When everything else shifts, He remains.

Notice that Abraham plants a tree - an act of hope and permanence - while worshipping the eternal God. Rooted in the Everlasting One, we can live with hope, planting for a future we may not see, trusting the God who outlasts every season. The eternal God who was Abraham's refuge is our refuge too, and "underneath are the everlasting arms" (Deut 33:27). Rest your changing life on the unchanging, Eternal God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you anchoring your changing life to the unchanging, Eternal God?
- How does knowing God is everlasting give you hope for the future?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Eternal God, everything in my life changes, but You never do. From everlasting to everlasting You are God. Anchor my shifting life to Your unchanging faithfulness, and let me rest in Your everlasting arms.
Amen.
